content.intended_use: Restricted deterministic first-order lower bound in hyperbolic space.

proofs.locator: Appendix A.1 pp.17–19 and A.2 pp.19–25
map: Eq. (7) and Lemma 24, pp.19–20: sinh(r_k)=sin(theta)^k sinh(r), and r_k>=r/2 through the stated budget.
Lemmas 25–26, pp.20–21: H_k is the residual totally geodesic submanifold; S_k is its sphere of radius r_k about y_k, and y_k is the closest point in I_k to x* in S_k.
Lemma 27, pp.22–23: boundary L_k contains I_k and x*; B_(k+1) lies in C_k=intersection_(z in S_(k+1))L_(k,z); the required centers belong to the penalty halfspaces.

Lemma 28, pp.23–24: for y in I_k, a subgradient ghat of dist(.,L_k)/cos(theta) makes ghat-log_y(x*)/dist(y,x*) tangent to I_(k+1). The source uses ghat=-sin(theta_y)P_(y_k->y)V_k/(cos(theta)||V_k||), with theta_y=angle(log_y(y_(k+1)),log_y(x*)); Eq. (11)–(13) give cancellation.
Eq. (14), p.24, declares global geodesic convexity and M-Lipschitzness. Lemma 27 and p.25 give x* in every L_i and f*=0.

p.25 induction: at x_(k-1) in all halfspaces all penalties vanish, so the selected penalty subgradient is active in the maximum. Lemma 28 supplies a subgradient of f tangent to I_k. A1 keeps x_k in I_k, A2 ensures previous halfspaces, and I_k subset I_ell subset boundary L_ell ensures later halfspaces. Thus f(x_k)=dist(x_k,x*)>=r_k>=r/2. Theorem 29 states the resulting guarantee.

source_wording_issues.issue: The source initially writes gap=r_k, but its subsequent derivation establishes dist(x_k,x*)>=r_k. This record asserts only the inequality.
The source writes the historical gspan equals I_k. Its argument uses containment to obtain x_k in I_k; equality is not asserted here.
The displayed Theorem 29 does not separately restate d>=2. This record retains that standing domain and does not resolve the possible d=1 empty maximum.
source_wording_issues.locator: PDF p.4 standing convention and p.19 parameter choice

assumptions: A is a deterministic first-order algorithm. A1: x_0=o and x_k in gspan(x_0,...,x_(k-1),g_0,...,g_(k-1)) for all k>=1; vector arguments denote tangency requirements at their query points.
A2: on the specified Oracle for this f, x_k in intersection_(ell=0,...,k-1)L_ell for every k<=d-1; the intersection is unrestricted at k=0.
Use the globally geodesically convex, globally M-Lipschitz Eq. (14) function above, with x* in S_(d-1). No smoothness or strong convexity assumption is required.
statement.conclusion: For every k=0,...,T-1, f(x_k)-f*=dist(x_k,x*)>=r_k>=r/2=epsilon M r. Moreover f*=f(x*)=0 and x* lies in B(o,r).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Work in H^d of curvature -1. Let o=x_ref, y_0=o, I_0={o}, r_0=r, S_0=boundary B(o,r), and choose an orthonormal basis e_i^(0) of T_o H^d. For k=1,...,d-1 define Delta_(k-1)=artanh(cos(theta)tanh(r_(k-1))), r_k=arsinh(sin(theta)sinh(r_(k-1))), y_k=exp_(y_(k-1))(Delta_(k-1)e_k^(k-1)), and e_i^(k)=P_(y_(k-1)->y_k)e_i^(k-1) for i=1,...,d. Set I_k=gspan(y_0,...,y_k), the minimal totally geodesic submanifold containing these points, and S_k={x in S_(k-1): angle(e_k^(k-1),log_(y_(k-1))(x))=theta}. Fix x* in S_(d-1). For k=0,...,d-2 define gtilde_k=-e_(k+1)^(k)/cos(theta), V_k=-gtilde_k-log_(y_k)(x*)/dist(y_k,x*), and L_k=exp_(y_k){v in T_(y_k)H^d: <V_k,v> >=0}. Let f(x)=dist(x,x*)+max_(i=0,...,d-2) dist(x,L_i)/cos(theta), exactly Eq. (14).
statement.parameter_domains: r>0; 0<epsilon<=1/(4sqrt(2)); zeta_r=r/tanh(r); theta=arccos(4epsilon) in (0,pi/2); M=2/cos(theta)=1/(2epsilon); T=d=floor(zeta_r/(32epsilon^2))>=2. The standing dimension convention on p.4 is retained; the possible d=1 empty-maximum case is excluded.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every parameter choice in the stated domain and every such construction with fixed x* in S_(d-1), for any deterministic algorithm A satisfying A1 and A2 on the specified trajectory, there exists an exact first-order Oracle for this fixed f with the stated queried-iterate guarantee. No randomized Algorithm guarantee is asserted.
